replacement: “Oh, by the way,” Ivan went on, as though he hadn’t heard his brother, “I met a Bulgarian in Moscow recently. He told me about the atrocities the Turks and Circassians are committing all over Bulgaria. They’re afraid of a general uprising of the Slavs. They burn villages, kill, rape women and children. They nail prisoners to fences by the ears and leave them there until morning, and in the morning they hang them. All sorts of things you can’t imagine. We sometimes speak of bestial cruelty, but that’s a great injustice and an insult to the beasts. No beast can ever be as cruel as a man, so artistically cruel. A tiger only tears and gnaws. That’s all he can do. It would never occur to him to nail people up by the ears, even if he could. These Turks enjoyed torturing children, too. They cut unborn babies out of their mothers’ wombs. They tossed infants into the air and caught them on their bayonets in front of their mothers. Doing it in front of the mothers was what gave the sport its zest. Here is another scene I found very interesting. Picture a trembling mother holding her baby, with a ring of invading Turks around her. They’ve thought up an entertainment. They fuss over the baby and laugh to make it laugh. It works, and the baby laughs. At that moment a Turk aims a pistol four inches from the baby’s face. The baby laughs with delight and reaches out its little hands for the pistol. And he pulls the trigger in the baby’s face and blows out its brains. Artistic, isn’t it? Turks are especially fond of sweets, they say, by the way.”
“Just as he did with God, then?” said Alyosha.
